reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides a practical Coinbase tutorial covering funding, cryptocurrency purchases and sales, withdrawals, and transfers to an external wallet. It includes warnings about retail-investor losses, platform and wallet security risks, and the FTX bankruptcy. Referrals and Coinbase learning-reward discussions, including an external quiz-answer site, are presented within the tutorial with affiliate disclosure, while the available video evidence does not establish whether any linked service is safe or whether any reward was received.

if you are planning to touch crypto, just know that there is a good chance that you will lose money ya?
After that, just select the account that you want to transfer from and the transfer amount.
First, look for the crypto that you want. Then click on BYE. Enter the amount that you want to buy. Make sure you're paying with your SGD wallet.
Next, you'll need to enter the destination address. So let's head over to Ledger Live to look for the wallet address.

opening.argument: The video links a concrete cryptocurrency reward to viewer action: viewers are told that completing Coinbase lessons and quizzes can earn “up to $10 in free cryptos,” then are directed to an external website containing the quiz answers. That turns the educational framing into a low-barrier acquisition path: use the linked answers, complete the process, and obtain a digital asset. The video also supplies numerous Coinbase and other financial-service links, making the reward discussion part of a broader solicitation ecosystem rather than a detached explanation.

I've found a website which has all the quiz answers, which I'll link down below so you can just refer to that
► Coinbase (free $10) https://kvli.link/coinbase ► Ledger https://kvli.link/ledger ► Trezor https://kvli.link/trezor

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not neutralize the explicit reward funnel. The video does not merely mention a reward; it explains the action required, offers a shortcut to the answers, and provides promotional links. Its warning language is compatible with solicitation because viewers are still instructed how to fund an account, buy crypto, and move it to a wallet.

I will show you how to fund your account, buy your crypto, sell it and withdraw the money back out.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The reward passage does not promise guaranteed payment or establish that anyone received it; it describes Coinbase’s stated learning program and says the amount is “up to $10.” The video expressly warns that crypto is dangerous and that viewers may lose money, while the affiliate disclosure identifies compensation from partnering websites rather than concealing the commercial relationship.

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: crypto acquisition, a free-crypto claim, external links, referral codes, and an invitation to move viewers through exchange and wallet workflows. The description advertises “free $10,” “free $25,” discounts, and multiple financial services, while the narration directs viewers to deposit funds, buy crypto, and transfer it externally. Presented together, these signals make the content function like a broad acquisition campaign, with the reward and referral offers lowering resistance to participation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the video contains warnings and operational steps does not remove the cumulative red flags. A viewer is still shown where to deposit money, how to buy crypto, and where to find external wallets, alongside free-asset offers and referral links. That combination can encourage participation even when risk language is present.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals do not establish deception. The narration emphasizes that crypto may cause losses, explains that platforms are not completely safe, recommends testing with a small amount, and says not to keep assets on the exchange. The external links are also disclosed as affiliate or referral links, so their presence alone does not prove a fraudulent offer.

opening.argument: Although styled as education, the video repeatedly steers viewers toward participation: it gives a step-by-step deposit procedure, demonstrates buying and selling, recommends external wallets, advertises Ledger and Trezor links, and ends with a reward and quiz-answer referral. The description expands this into a long list of financial, payment, investing, and lifestyle offers. That breadth makes the tutorial’s practical role promotional: it reduces friction for opening, funding, trading, and claiming incentives rather than simply explaining cryptocurrency concepts.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational label cannot answer the specific promotional conduct. The speaker does not stop at general information: viewers are shown the exact funding, purchase, sale, withdrawal, and wallet-transfer workflow, then sent to linked products and a Telegram group. Affiliate disclosure may identify compensation, but it does not make the steering purely educational.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A practical demonstration can still be educational without being a scam. The tutorial explains the mechanics and repeatedly introduces limitations: higher simple-trade fees, platform failure risk, wallet hacking risk, and the possibility of losing money. The description also expressly says the material is not investment advice and identifies affiliate compensation.
